25.0.s.en: 1. A song of thanksgiving to God:

25.0.0.en: 1 O LORD, thou art my God; I will exalt thee, I will praise thy name; for thou hast done wonderful things; thy counsels of old are faithfulness and truth. 2 For thou hast made of a city an heap; of a defenced city a ruin: a palace of strangers to be no city; it shall never be built. 3 Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee. 4 For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall. 5 Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers, as the heat in a dry place; even the heat with the shadow of a cloud: the branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low.

25.0.1.en: The eyes of the prophet Isaiah were opened to the Kingdom of Christ, so his heart overflowed with exultation and his tongue was loosed to praise God for His work of salvation. After prophesying of bitter chastisements, he became a psalmist offering psalms of thanksgiving to God. The secret of his praise and thanksgiving to God is:

25.0.2.en: A. The fulfillment of God's words and His faithful and true promises: “O LORD, thou art my God; I will exalt thee, I will praise thy name; for thou hast done wonderful things; thy counsels of old are faithfulness and truth” [1]. The prophet realized that the secret of salvation lies in God's faithful promises and the wonderful work of His hands. Therefore St. Irenaeus comments on this song, saying: [We see here that we are not saved by ourselves but by the help of God.]

25.0.3.en: We praise God and give thanks to Him for His wonderful eternal divine purposes, for from of old He has been concerned for our salvation, before we existed, because we were in His mind, the object of His love.

25.1.0.en: B. The destruction of evil (Babylon): “For thou hast made of a city an heap; of a defenced city a ruin: a palace of strangers to be no city; it shall never be built” [2].

25.1.1.en: Our salvation by the divine arm is accomplished by doing away with evil, that is, with the city of Babylon, arrogant and full of confusion, which embraces the Antichrist. It is as though the secret of our praise is the rising of the Kingdom of Christ, which is accompanied by the collapse of the kingdom of the devil, the opponent of the truth, the shattering of his city and the demolition of his palace.

25.1.2.en: Perhaps the city here refers to the enemy of good's dominion over a community, the village refers to his dominion over a smaller group such as the family, and the palace refers to his possession of the heart. For the enemy of good works on every level to reign through the community, the family or the individual... and our Christ also resists him on every level in order to demolish every trace of his kingdom.

25.1.3.en: As for calling the soul that the enemy dominates a “palace of strangers” or a “palace of foreigners,” it is because the enemy of good and his angels occupy the soul as strangers and foreigners, possessing what is not theirs; it is God's good creation into which they have crept.

25.1.4.en: Perhaps also the demolition of the city, the village or the palace refers to the demolition of our old man with all his works for the sake of the continual renewal of our inner man in the image of his Creator (2 Cor 4:16).

25.2.0.en: C. Preaching: Among the things that gladden the heart and fill it with praise is that the rising of the inner kingdom of Christ, with the demolition of the kingdom of the enemy of good in us, is accompanied by witness, or preaching, of the work of God and the Gospel of His salvation, so that many souls are drawn and a strong Church arises, strong not in numbers but because of her almighty Christ who dwells in her. The prophet says: “Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee” [3].

25.2.1.en: Our souls exult in God's strong people, who carry within them the power of His Resurrection that overcomes death, so that they live as “terrible ones” (mighty men of valor) who practice the fear of God. As it is said of them: “and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army” (Ezek 37:10); “terrible as an army with banners” (Song 6:10).

25.2.2.en: When the city of Babylon collapses in us, the defenced village of the devil is broken down and his palace is laid waste, the Lord reigns in order to raise from us a strong people, terrifying to the enemy... What is this terrifying people but the sanctification of soul and body, thought, words and feelings, even to the shadow of man? Did not diseases flee from the shadow of the Apostle Peter (Acts 5:15)? Did not demons and evil spirits come out at the mere sight of the handkerchiefs of the Apostle Paul?

25.3.0.en: D. Justice for the wronged: “For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall. Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers, as the heat in a dry place...” [4-5].

25.3.1.en: Mankind groans under the law of injustice that has prevailed over it since sin entered it. Therefore God Himself comes forward as a practical secret of consolation, upholding every wounded soul, offering Himself as strength and stronghold to the poor and needy in the time of distress, a refuge from the floods (the storms), and a shadow from the heat while the blast of the mighty man is like a storm against a wall. It is as though God, in His surpassing love and fatherly care, presents Himself to His believers according to their needs, becoming everything to them for their peace, their edification and their fulfillment; He is the strength, the stronghold, the refuge, the dark cloud, the bread that came down from heaven, and so on...

25.4.s.en: 2. The feast of the New Covenant:

25.4.0.en: 6 And in this mountain shall the LORD of hosts make unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined. 7 And he will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations. 8 He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken it. 9 And it shall be said in that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the LORD; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation.

25.4.1.en: The Word of God the Savior comes to every soul to be the One who satisfies its needs and gives it peace and strength against the evil enemy, so that the soul enjoys the new life in Christ as a joyful and perpetual feast. This feast is in truth the satisfying evangelical life offered to all peoples, which he describes here as follows:

25.4.2.en: A. A universal feast: “And in this mountain shall the LORD of hosts make unto all people a feast...” [6]. The door has been opened wide to all peoples to enjoy the word of God, His covenants, His promises, His laws and His works of salvation, especially communion in the Eucharist (the Body and Blood of the Lord); God's gifts are no longer the monopoly of a particular people or a special race.

25.4.3.en: The Lord Christ declares the universality of the call by saying: “Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage” (Mt 22:9).

25.4.4.en: B. A rich feast, which he called “a feast of fat things” [6]. What is this rich feast, or rich festival, but the sacrament of the Eucharist, where believers from all peoples join the heavenly beings in praise, and the doors of heaven are opened before them, or rather the Church becomes heaven, so that the believers may enjoy the broken Body of the Lord and His precious Blood for their salvation and fulfillment?

25.4.5.en: * [“The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want...” (Ps 23)]

25.4.6.en: Hear about the nature of the sacraments that you have received. Hear what David says to you... How did he begin his psalm, saying that he is no longer in want of anything? Why? Because whoever partakes of the Body of Christ hungers no more.

25.4.7.en: St. Ambrose * Those who were deprived of earthly blessings because of their young age are given heavenly gifts richly, to the full, so that they have the right to sing with joy, saying: “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want” (Ps 23:1).

25.4.8.en: St. Didymus the Blind * This table is the support of our souls, the bond of our mind, the foundation of our hope, our salvation, our light and our life.

25.4.9.en: * When you see the table prepared before you, say to yourself:

25.4.10.en: Because of His Body I shall no longer be dust and ashes, nor a prisoner, but free!

25.4.11.en: Because of this (Body) I hope for heaven, and I receive the heavenly good things, the immortal life, the portion of the angels, and conversation with Christ.

25.4.12.en: This Body was nailed with nails and scourged, and death can no longer overpower it!

25.4.13.en: It is the Body that was stained with blood and pierced, and from it came out the two springs that save the world: the spring of blood and the spring of water.

25.4.14.en: St. John Chrysostom C. A spiritually joyful feast: “A feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined” [6]. The wine signifies spiritual joy; and its being refined, or pure, means that it does not take away man's consciousness and make him drunk, but gives him spiritual gladness.

25.4.15.en: * The cup of the Lord makes us drunk in a certain way, as Noah drank a cup of intoxicating wine in the Book of Genesis, but the drunkenness of the cup of the Lord and His blood is not like the drunkenness of the wine of the world... For the cup of the Lord makes those who drink it sober and brings their thoughts back to spiritual wisdom; it moves man from the taste of the world to the understanding of God... It frees the soul and removes its gloom from it... It gives rest to the soul, for it offers it the joy of divine goodness in place of the heart's dark depression under the weight of the burdens of sin.

25.5.0.en: The Martyr Cyprian D. A heavenly feast: through it the covering is uncovered and the veil of the letter is removed, so that the partakers enter heaven itself and come to know its mysteries, which were hidden from all the sons of men. “And he will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations” [7].

25.5.1.en: * The people who have been purified and filled with wondrous gifts begin to walk toward the altar, saying: “To the house of God we go, God gladdens our youth...” They hasten toward the heavenly feast.

25.5.2.en: St. Ambrose * Every time we serve the liturgy of this sacrifice, it is fitting for us to count ourselves as those who are in heaven.

25.6.0.en: Father Theodoret E. A life-giving feast: “He will swallow up death in victory” [8].

25.6.1.en: * Through (this sacrifice) we, who are by nature mortal, await immortality, and we, who are corruptible, incorruption, and in place of the earth and its evils we receive the blessings and joys of heaven.

25.6.2.en: Father Theodoret * Lest we be puffed up, supposing that life is of ourselves, and become arrogant toward God... we must know by experience that we receive eternal life not from our nature but by the power of this Supreme Being, “the Eucharist.”

25.6.3.en: St. Irenaeus F. A glorious feast: “And the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken it” [8]. For He gives His believers rest in Him through the holy life, or through their enjoyment of the righteousness of Christ. If tears crept into all mankind through its disobedience, our union with God in His Son by the Holy Spirit gives us steadfastness in Christ, who was obedient to the Father; so He removes from us the burden of our disobedience and dries our inner tears, granting the soul glories within, which we experience in our temporal life as a pledge of the eternal heavenly glory.

25.6.4.en: Our life is a striving and a struggle against the powers of darkness, a continual battle whose field is the inner heart, but our Christ gives us the overcoming and the victory; He binds up every wound and wipes away every tear.

25.6.5.en: * The sacramental table is the Body of the Lord, who supports us against our lusts and against Satan.

25.6.6.en: Truly Satan trembles before those who partake of these mysteries with reverence.

25.7.0.en: 10 For in this mountain shall the hand of the LORD rest, and Moab shall be trodden down under him, even as straw is trodden down for the dunghill. 11 And he shall spread forth his hands in the midst of them, as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim: and he shall bring down their pride together with the spoils of their hands. 12 And the fortress of the high fort of thy walls shall he bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust.

25.7.1.en: As the believers, who overcome sorrow, bitterness, tears, and even death, exult through the free feast of salvation, they say: “Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us” [9]. Our joy lies in our salvation from our enemies, that is, from the devil and all his hosts and all his evil works. For the glory of the children of God is accompanied by the shame of the powers of darkness, which are symbolized here by Moab. “And Moab shall be trodden down under him, even as straw is trodden down for the dunghill. And he shall spread forth his hands in the midst of them, as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim: and he shall bring down their pride together with the spoils of their hands. And the fortress of the high fort of thy walls shall he bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust” [10-11].

25.7.2.en: If the powers of darkness have exalted themselves over the children of God and supposed that they were able to humble them, God by the cross demolished their strongholds and brought them down to the abyss, granting us authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and all the powers of darkness; we tread them as straw is trodden for use in building materials (in making mud bricks). It is as though those powers that were the cause of our destruction are turned, through the saving work of God, into a despised and humbled instrument under the feet, used for the edification of our souls; for without the devil we would not be crowned.

25.7.3.en: The secret of the enemy's destruction is his pride, for he counted himself fortified by impregnable walls, but God brings these walls down to the ground, so that the enemy's weakness is exposed and the truth of his helplessness before our God is revealed.

26.0.s.en: 1. A psalm urging trust in God:

26.0.0.en: 1 In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah; We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks. 2 Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in. 3 Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee. 4 Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is the rock of ages.

26.0.1.en: The psalm begins with the introduction: “In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah” [1]. It is the song of the New Covenant; it was not possible for the men of the Old Covenant to sing it, and so he says “in that day.” The blessings enjoyed by the ancient people, such as the return from captivity, do not bring lasting joy except insofar as they are a type of the joyful salvation accomplished by our return from the captivity of sin through the work of the cross.

26.0.2.en: This psalm is a song for Jerusalem, the city of God, because of the strength and fortification she enjoyed, with open gates, and righteousness, faithfulness and peace for her inhabitants...

26.0.3.en: “We have a strong city” [1] means Jerusalem, a type of the heavenly Jerusalem, and also the Church of the New Covenant, as the city of God in which the Lord Himself dwells with His people.

26.0.4.en: “Salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks” [1]; God's saving works are the walls of the city and its instruments of war, so the enemy of good cannot storm it. He may fight against it and try to entice it, but he will not be able to overcome it so long as it is faithful to the Lord.

26.0.5.en: The Fathers of the Church, especially St. Augustine, often spoke of our inner life as the Church of Christ, the heavenly city of the Lord. In its essence this city is the dwelling of God, who is Love, with men; love is its founder, its treasure, its language and its law... The city of the Lord is the city of love!

26.0.6.en: * When you attain perfect knowledge and become, through love, the throne of God, you become heaven!

26.0.7.en: The heaven that we see with our eyes when we look up is not very precious to God; the holy souls are the heaven of God...

26.0.9.en: It is clear that Zion is the city of God; and what is the city of God but the holy Church? When men love one another and love God who dwells in them, they become the city of God... For it is plainly written: “God is love” (1 Jn 4:8). Whoever is filled with love is filled with God.

26.0.10.en: * We have learned that there is a city of God, whose Founder inspired in us the love that makes us desire citizenship in it.

26.0.11.en: St. Augustine * In love God established every soul to be His fortified city and His holy heavens; He established her as His heavenly bride, united with Him, having the same possibilities as her bridegroom the Savior, who ascended into the heavens, and the everlasting doors were opened before Him that the King of glory might enter in (Ps 24:7-10). She is also His bride who carries His righteousness and faithfulness; the doors of heaven are opened before her, that she may sit at the right hand of her bridegroom the King and in His bosom, and no power can prevent her from passing through the heavenly places until she reaches His throne. She is like Queen Esther, who passed through all the doors of the palace to reach the king, who stretched out to her his golden scepter that she might enter to him, and he caressed her and listened to her petition.

26.1.0.en: Isaiah perhaps enjoyed these prophetic feelings when he saw in the Spirit those returning from captivity entering the gates of Jerusalem opened before them, entering as in a procession of victory or a festal procession of joy in the Lord. He said: “Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in” [2].

26.1.1.en: * “Lift up your gates, O ye princes” (Ps 24:7); let us go straight to heaven.

26.1.2.en: May the prophet's trumpet sound aloud: “Lift up, O ye rulers of the air, the gates that you have set up in the minds of men...”

26.1.3.en: St. Augustine St. Ambrose comments on the phrase “Be ye lift up, ye everlasting gates; and the King of glory shall come in” (Ps 24:7), saying:

26.1.4.en: [They found that a new way must be prepared before the face of this new “Victor,” for He is always, as He was, greater than others; but because the gates of righteousness, which are the gates of the Old and New Testaments, in which the heavens are opened, are everlasting gates, therefore they are truly unchanging, yet they were lifted up, because the One who enters them is not a man but the whole world in the person of the Savior of all...

26.1.5.en: When (the angels) perceived the approach of the Lord of all, the first conqueror of death and the only Victor, they commanded the (heavenly) hosts to lift up the gates, saying in rapture and devotion... “Be ye lift up, ye everlasting gates; and the King of glory shall come in”].

26.1.6.en: Thus, as heaven is opened before the believers united with our Lord Jesus, and they are raised with Him to His heavens, they live here in true peace and trust in the Savior. Therefore the prophet says:

26.2.0.en: “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee” [3]. A wonderful expression of the sure assurance that God gives to His believers who are faithful to Him, for He gives them peace followed by peace until they reach the final victory because of their reliance on Him.

26.3.0.en: By “whose mind is stayed” he means those with a firm purpose, or a balanced, unshakable mind, whom the storms of events do not cause to lose their confidence in God their Savior, Jehovah the rock of ages (Isa 26:4; Ps 18:31): “Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is the rock of ages” [4].

26.3.1.en: * Wretched is the people that turns away from God... But our own peace we enjoy now with God by faith, and we shall enjoy it eternally with Him by sight.

26.3.2.en: St. Augustine * Everyone ought to reform himself, and be at peace with himself, and there should be no division in his conscience. For if a man is reconciled with the whole world while he is divided against himself, his reconciliation is of no benefit. But he who reforms his soul and is at peace with himself is like one who has made peace with the whole world, and he is honored in the eyes of the Master of all.

26.3.3.en: * Have pity, O Lord, on the soul that has been kindled with Your love, for she is the dwelling of peace; so leave no trace of sin in the conscience, the place of Your dwelling, but burn it with the fire of Your love.

26.4.0.en: 5 For he bringeth down them that dwell on high; the lofty city, he layeth it low; he layeth it low, even to the ground; he bringeth it even to the dust. 6 The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy.

26.4.1.en: “For he bringeth down them that dwell on high” [5-6].

26.4.2.en: If Babylon has exalted herself and supposed that she is on high, the Lord will bring her down to the dust, to make her trodden by the feet of the poor, whom she had previously trampled with her feet. This is the end of every proud person who opposes the truth, for he drinks of the same cup that he offered to others.

26.4.3.en: God's constant work is to glorify humble, lowly Jerusalem and establish her as a city of His own, and to bring down proud Babylon. As St. Mary said: “He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away” (Lk 1:53).

26.4.4.en: * You taught me the ways of humility, through which men return to life, having fallen because of pride.

26.4.5.en: St. Augustine * By pride we lean upon the winds, and by it we thrust ourselves into the deep; so do not accept the disease of pride, lest the enemy rob you...

26.4.6.en: * In the humble man the spirit of wisdom rests.

26.5.s.en: 3. The Lord's support for His righteous ones:

26.5.0.en: 7 The way of the just is uprightness: thou, most upright, dost weigh the path of the just. 8 Yea, in the way of thy judgments, O LORD, have we waited for thee; the desire of our soul is to thy name, and to the remembrance of thee. 9 With my soul have I desired thee in the night; yea, with my spirit within me will I seek thee early: for when thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness. 10 Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the LORD. 11 LORD, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see: but they shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people; yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them. 12 LORD, thou wilt ordain peace for us: for thou also hast wrought all our works for us. 13 O LORD our God, other lords beside thee have had dominion over us: but by thee only will we make mention of thy name. 14 They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish. 15 Thou hast increased the nation, O LORD, thou hast increased the nation: thou art glorified: thou hast enlarged all the ends of the earth. 16 LORD, in trouble have they visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them.

26.5.1.en: In this psalm the prophet presents to us a wonderful analysis of the life of the righteous man, who finds his delight, his protection and his glory in the Lord; and at the same time he calls us to secret prayer in the closet, with attention to God's judgments and commandments and obedience to Him, to enjoy His free salvation.

26.6.0.en: A. God's judgments or commandments are not a burden on the soul of the righteous man; rather they are the cause of his uprightness, so he seeks them and desires them with joy and gladness of heart, saying: “In the way of thy judgments... have we waited for thee” [8]. It is as though the commandment, or the word of God, is the object of the soul's hope, delight and joy. As the psalmist says: “I have rejoiced in the way of thy testimonies, as much as in all riches... I will delight myself in thy statutes... Thy testimonies also are my delight” (Ps 119:14, 16, 24).

26.6.1.en: Perhaps the secret of the righteous man's joy and gladness in the commandment is that he discovers its depths and finds it to be an encounter with Christ the Word of God and an enjoyment of Him as a mystery of salvation and life. As St. Augustine says: [We understand that there is no way swifter or safer or shorter or higher than Christ with regard to the testimonies of God, He “in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge” (Col 2:3). Therefore he (the psalmist) says that he finds in Him great delight as in all riches. These are the testimonies by which (Christ) assured us how far He loves us...]

26.6.2.en: B. The secret of the righteous man's joy is his union with God his Savior and his clinging to His holy name and remembrance: “The desire of our soul is to thy name, and to the remembrance of thee. With my soul have I desired thee in the night; yea, with my spirit within me will I seek thee early” [8-9]. The soul realizes that in the night of this world she needs the light of the Savior to shine upon her, and indeed within her. She seeks Him in the night because she has tasted what is most bitter throughout the toil of the day and its unceasing pains, so she wants to meet Him within her, to find in Him her rest, her peace and her fulfillment, as the desire of her soul. She asks Him that she may enjoy all His kisses (Song 1:2), and she converses with Him, saying: “His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem” (Song 5:16).

26.6.3.en: The soul desires Him that she may cling to Him through all the night of this world, until eternity dawns upon her and she remains with Him in His embrace forever.

26.6.4.en: She seeks Him within her; she searches for Him and finds Him seeking her; she rises early to Him and finds Him rising early to her. She converses with Him: “Early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is; to see thy power and thy glory, so as I have seen thee in the sanctuary” (Ps 63:1-2). And He answers: “I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me. Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness” (Prov 8:17-18).

26.7.0.en: C. The end of the righteous man is his enjoyment of the divine glory, which the wicked are deprived of, as the prophet says: “In the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the LORD” [10]. The righteous man enjoys the glory and majesty of the Lord, and the splendor of the Lord is reflected upon him so that he becomes an icon of Him, while the wicked is deprived of the enjoyment of this eternal gift.

26.7.1.en: * Blessed, thrice blessed, indeed many times blessed are those who are counted worthy to see that glory! Of this the prophet says: “Let the wicked be taken away, that he may not see the glory of the Lord” [10 LXX].

26.7.2.en: God does not allow any one of us to be taken away or kept from seeing Him. For if we do not enjoy this, a time will come when we say to ourselves: “It would have been better for us never to have been born.” For why do we live? And why do we breathe? What are we if we fail to enjoy the sight of this and are not granted to behold the Lord? If those who do not see the light of the sun count life as more bitter than death, what will be the state of those deprived of such a light?

26.7.3.en: St. John Chrysostom * It is fitting for us to understand that it is for the sake of this perfection that “we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is” (1 Jn 3:2). This gift is granted when it is said: “Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you” (Mt 25:34). Then the wicked are taken away so that they do not see the majesty of the Lord, and those on the left go away into everlasting punishment, while those on the right enter into life eternal.

26.7.4.en: * John says: “Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is” (1 Jn 3:2). This likeness begins to take shape in us from now, while the inner man is renewed day by day after the image of his Creator.

26.7.5.en: St. Augustine Thus God becomes the secret of the glory of His righteous ones, not only in the world to come, but their glory begins now within them, as they behold the glory and majesty of God as a pledge of meeting Him eternally face to face; and God Himself becomes the cause of the deprivation of the wicked; He is the King of peace to His believers and a consuming fire to those who deny Him. The Apostle says: “To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life” (2 Cor 2:16). Therefore the prophet Isaiah continues, saying:

26.7.6.en: “LORD, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see: but they shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people; yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them.

26.8.0.en: LORD, thou wilt ordain peace for us: for thou also hast wrought (rendered) all our works for us” [11-12].

26.9.0.en: The Lord lifts up His hand to discipline His children, and gives them peace and growth, since they receive it as discipline for their sins; but for the wicked, the punishment is a consuming fire that destroys them and makes their memory perish [14].

26.10.0.en: 17 Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs; so have we been in thy sight, O LORD. 18 We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth wind; we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen. 19 Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.

26.10.1.en: The prophet realizes the blessings of affliction for the people of God, saying: “Thou hast increased the nation, O LORD, thou hast increased the nation: thou art glorified: thou hast enlarged all the ends of the earth. LORD, in trouble have they visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them” [15-16]. It is as though discipline causes distress and weariness outwardly, but it leads to continual growth and expansion in glory.

26.10.2.en: The secret of strength is not in affliction but in the hidden hand of God, able to raise from the dead. The prophet saw his people like a woman writhing with the pains of labor, who bears with effort and then brings forth wind, that is, the pains of labor end in nothing; but if God intervenes, then even if man in his sufferings reaches death, He is able to give him resurrection, to give him a new, risen life full of joy and praise.

26.10.3.en: The wicked suffer as in the state of childbirth, but they bring forth out of themselves (the ego) wind, or empty pride; but the children of God suffer and bring forth by the work of the Spirit, in likeness to God. It is as though pain apart from the Lord Christ gives birth to wind, but in Christ it brings forth resurrection!

26.10.4.en: The prophet says: “Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs; so have we been in thy sight, O LORD. We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth wind; we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth... Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust...” [17-19].

26.10.5.en: The psalmist says: “For, lo, the kings were assembled... They saw it, and so they marvelled; they were troubled, and hasted away. Fear took hold upon them there, and pain, as of a woman in travail” (Ps 48:4-6). St. Augustine sees that the kings are the company of believers who conceive from the fear of God and enter into labor to bring forth salvation through faith. When we hear of their sufferings we expect a new birth, in which the old man dies with all his works and the new man is born in the image of his Creator.

26.10.6.en: St. Augustine addresses the virgin soul joined to Christ her Bridegroom, saying: [It is well for you, O virgin soul... By your virginity you keep in your heart what you have borne again (the new man), and keep in your body what you have brought forth, since you conceived by the fear of the Lord and gave birth to the spirit of salvation.]

26.11.s.en: 5. God is the Savior of His people:

26.11.0.en: 20 Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast. 21 For, behold, the LORD cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.

26.11.1.en: If God is angry, it is not to avenge Himself but to discipline, declaring His love for our salvation; therefore He called the period of His anger “a little moment,” which passes quickly, as He waits to reward His believers, while the wicked drink from the cup of their evil what they have filled for themselves.

26.11.2.en: Our life with all its pains is “a little moment” that passes quickly with us, not to be compared with a glorious eternity without end. Therefore St. Augustine says: [There is a rest in death, of which the prophet speaks, saying: “Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast.”]

26.11.3.en: How beautiful that the hymn of the Resurrection before us should be concluded with the wonderful phrase: “For, behold, the LORD cometh out of his place to punish” [26]. He is a heavenly Father who longs not to punish; if He disciplines, it is as one who has come out of his place, that is, out of mercy full of compassion and tenderness. Our iniquity and disobedience make Him as one who comes out of His place to punish... even in His coming out He seeks to gather us to Himself, to bring us back to the throne of His mercy.
